findings.finding: Only the exact #[cfg(test)] on a mod item counts. A mod under cfg(all(test, ...)), cfg(test) on a non-mod item, and an inner #![cfg(test)] are not seen as test-only. Under such code a reference to a dev-only workspace crate gives no edge, which is a false negative, not a false edge. cfg(any(test, feature)) is correctly not test-only. In crates/ryo today: one mod-level all(test, ...) (benchmark local/fixtures.rs:2 'mod pins_test'), which names no dev-only workspace crate (tempfile is external, ryo_benchmark_contracts is a normal dependency), and one fn (languages/python/benchmarks/linters/ruff/host_policy.rs:38). The one #![cfg(test)] file (core cross_file/fixtures.rs:2) is also declared under #[cfg(test)]. 178 non-mod cfg(test) items exist, and none names a dev-only workspace crate. No edge is lost in the real tree, so this is not a check 3 FAIL. Close it by reading cfg predicates (all(...) containing test, with no any/not escape) or by adding a lint that forbids such forms.
